metaDescription: Six countertop nugget ice makers compared on tank access, touchscreen versus buttons, carry handles and descaling, for tight counters and daily use.
expertTake: The Euhomy 2026 Upgraded dual-pump model is the best pick for its five-minute first batch and sensible tank handling. The Silonn 33 lb is the value pick for a compact body with a scoop. Skip countertop nugget machines if you want near-silent operation, because every auger model makes some noise. Measure your cabinet clearance first. Pre-chilling the fill water also speeds the first batch.
introParagraphs: A countertop nugget ice maker brings soft, chewable pellet ice to a kitchen without plumbing. The machine freezes a layer of water onto a cold cylinder and scrapes it into pellets with an auger, which is why the ice is so soft and why the machine is louder than a bullet-ice unit. Many owners say it is the appliance they use most in summer.

On a counter, what matters most is how you fill it, how you reach the tank and how much room it eats. Pull-out tanks, top covers, touchscreens and handles change daily life more than a few pounds of rated output. This guide compares those practical choices across six machines. Treat output ratings as ceilings, not promises.

products.name: Euhomy 2026 Upgraded Countertop Nugget Ice Maker 35 lb Dual-Pump
products.description:
This Euhomy model combines a rated 35 pounds per day with first ice in about five minutes and a dual-pump design. The dual pump is the notable upgrade: it supports water handling in the machine so refilling and draining are faster, and it reduces the chance of the water circuit running dry.

A five-minute first batch is at the quick end of the nugget class. The ice is soft sonic crushed ice, the style many people chew. Compared with the Frigidaire touchscreen model, it offers a similar output without the touch panel, and compared with the Silonn 44 lb, it makes less ice but is quicker to the first batch.

Like every auger machine, it hums and crunches, and rated output is a best case in a cool room. Use filtered water, descale every month or two, and leave clearance around the machine. Empty the tank if it sits idle for days. Pre-chill the water and keep the room cool for the best output. A short empty cycle before first use helps flush any factory residue.
products.bestFor: Kitchens that want quick nugget ice with a modern water circuit.
pros: First ice in about five minutes
cons: Auger noise like every nugget machine

products.name: Frigidaire Touchscreen Nugget Ice Maker 33 lb Slate
products.description:
The Frigidaire swaps buttons for a touchscreen and gives the machine a slate finish that blends with modern kitchens. It is a sonic nugget maker with a stated 33 pound capacity from a familiar appliance brand.

Touch controls are easy to read but are a possible wear point in a steamy, splashy kitchen, so wipe them gently. Compared with the Euhomy 2026 model, it trades a little rated output for the look and brand name. Compared with the Silonn models, it costs more.

As with every nugget machine, descale on schedule and use filtered water. Keep a clearance of several inches around the body so the compressor can breathe. The slate finish hides fingerprints better than glossy plastic, though it can show water spots. Because the controls are a screen, keep the machine out of the direct splash zone beside a sink.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a familiar brand and a touchscreen control.
cons: Touch panel can wear with splashes
Higher price tier than value brands

products.name: Silonn Countertop Nugget Ice Maker 44 lb Front Pull-Out Tank
products.description:
The Silonn 44 lb has a front pull-out water tank, which means you refill by sliding the tank forward instead of lifting the machine or reaching behind it. For a countertop under a cabinet, that front access is the difference between filling in seconds and wrestling with the machine.

It is rated at 44 pounds per day, the highest output among the countertop picks, and offers a removable bin. Compared with the Euhomy 2026, it makes more ice but takes longer to the first batch. Compared with the Frigidaire, it lacks the touchscreen and the brand name.

A pull-out tank has seals that need occasional care. Descale regularly and wipe the tank. Pulling the tank forward also makes rinsing easier, so the tank is less likely to grow a film. Put a small tray under the machine in case the tank drips when removed. Expect it to be one of the heavier units, so choose the spot before you fill it.
products.bestFor: Counters under cabinets where front access matters.

products.name: Silonn Nugget Ice Maker 33 lb with Scoop
products.description:
The Silonn 33 lb is a straightforward nugget machine at a low-middle price tier, with a scoop included. A rated 33 pounds per day makes soft crushed chewable ice for daily use.

It lacks the headline features of the Euhomy dual-pump or the Silonn pull-out tank, which is why it costs less. Compared with the Kismile, it is similar in output but a touch cheaper.

Descale on schedule and use filtered water. The included scoop is a small convenience that saves buying one, and the compact body fits most counters. Owners who just want chewable ice for daily drinks tend to be happiest with this kind of simple machine. Treat it as the entry point: if you like nugget ice, it proves the idea cheaply.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want basic nugget ice.

products.name: EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker with Handle 34 lb Ready in 6 Min
products.description:
This EUHOMY adds a carry handle and a removable top cover to a 34 pound per day nugget maker. The handle makes moving the machine between a counter and a cabinet realistic, and the removable cover simplifies cleaning the interior.

First ice arrives in about six minutes. Compared with the Euhomy 2026, it lacks the dual pump but keeps the handle. Compared with the Silonn 44, it makes less ice.

An auto-cleaning cycle helps, but it does not remove scale. Descale regularly. The removable top cover is the feature that matters in year two, because lifting it lets you wipe the interior where scale and residue collect. The handle also makes draining the reservoir for storage far less awkward. Keep the cover seated firmly or the machine may refuse to run.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to move the machine and clean the interior easily.

products.name: Kismile Nugget Ice Maker 35 lb Stainless
products.description:
The Kismile is a portable stainless nugget maker rated at 35 pounds per day. The stainless body gives it a more premium look than plastic rivals.

It matches the Euhomy 2026's rated output but lacks the dual pump and the five-minute headline. Compared with the Frigidaire, it is less proven but offers metal.

Descale and keep clearance around it. Stainless wipes clean but shows fingerprints, so a soft microfiber cloth keeps it tidy. The portable label does not mean light, so place it where you can use it and leave it. Treat the maker's output rating as a ceiling for a cool room.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stainless nugget maker.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A front pull-out tank, as on the Silonn 44 lb, lets you refill without moving the machine. A top-fill or rear tank can be awkward under a cabinet. Measure the space above the machine. Measure the height with the lid open, since a lid that cannot lift is a common surprise under cabinets. Cabinets that sit about 18 inches above the counter are the usual problem, since a top-fill lid needs room to open.

Touchscreens like the Frigidaire's are easy to read but can fail with splashes. Buttons are simpler. Choose based on kitchen conditions. If your counter is near the sink, a touchscreen may take splashes you did not plan for. Look for a model with a clear water level indicator so you are not guessing when the tank is empty.

Nugget machines are heavy. A carry handle, as on the EUHOMY 34 lb, makes moving realistic. Without one, the machine tends to stay put. A machine you cannot lift is a machine you will not move, so choose a handle if you need to.

Ratings from 33 to 44 lb per day are best-case. First ice arrives in 5 to 10 minutes. A warm kitchen cuts output. Compare first-ice minutes with the number of guests you expect. The first batch is soft and wet, and quality improves as the cylinder reaches temperature.

Scale on the cylinder cuts output and flavor. Use filtered water and descale every month or two. Self-cleaning cycles do not remove scale. Hard water scales a machine quickly, so test your tap and consider a pitcher filter. Skipping descaling is the most common cause of lost output.

Auger machines hum and crunch. Leave several inches of clearance on every side so the compressor can breathe. A rubber mat under the machine absorbs vibration. Place the machine away from heat sources like ovens, which cut output.

specDecoder.meaning: Two water pumps that handle fill and drain. It reduces the chance of running dry.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Euhomy 2026 lists it. Check that the pump noise stays acceptable in your room.

specDecoder.meaning: A front-access water reservoir. A front tank saves lifting the machine.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Silonn 44 lb has one. Make sure the tank seals are intact after each refill.

specDecoder.meaning: A name for soft nugget ice. The names sonic, pebble and nugget describe the same soft ice.
specDecoder.watchFor: It is the same product as pebble ice.

specDecoder.meaning: Best-case output. Real output depends on room temperature.
specDecoder.watchFor: Lower in warm kitchens. Warm kitchens routinely give lower real numbers.

specDecoder.meaning: A lid that lifts off for cleaning. It makes cleaning faster.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EUHOMY 34 lb has one. Wipe the cover edge to keep the seal clean.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank and access
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed pull-out and top-fill designs for counters under cabinets. Owner reports about awkward refills shaped this weighting. A tank that is awkward to reach would be left half empty, so access mattered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared touchscreens with buttons for kitchen conditions. Splash exposure matters most near a sink.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 33 to 44 lb ratings and first-ice times. Marketing outputs were treated as ceilings. First-ice times of 5 to 10 minutes were treated as a convenience, not a performance guarantee.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited removable covers and weighed descaling. Cleaning access was weighted heavily because scale builds quickly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value by tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We ordered picks by relative price tier, from the Silonn 33 lb up to the Frigidaire. A lower tier only ranked well if it made ice reliably. No pick was promoted over a cheaper one without a concrete feature.

howToChoose.intro: Start with where the machine will live, because counter height and cabinet clearance change which model is practical.
Prices move, so these are relative tiers from the cheapest pick to the most expensive pick in this lineup.

cards.label: Touchscreen
cards.text: The Frigidaire is easy to read but may wear in splashes.

cards.label: Buttons
cards.text: The Euhomy, Silonn and Kismile models use simpler controls.

howToChoose.note: Choose buttons for longevity. If your kitchen is splashy, lean to buttons; if you want a clean modern look, lean touchscreen.

howToChoose.intro: Tank handling decides how annoying daily use feels, so compare access before output.

howToChoose.subheading: For Daily Coffee and Sodas Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Soft ice and a quick first batch so a glass is never far away. Chilled water speeds up the first batch.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Euhomy 2026 and Silonn 33 lb both make soft ice. Both suit a daily drink habit. The Euhomy 2026 also reaches the first batch quickest, which suits impatient guests.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a brand name and touchscreen. The Frigidaire pays off. The extra cost also buys a better chance of service support.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want basic nugget ice. The Silonn 33 lb covers it. You can always upgrade after a season. Basic nugget ice is the same product whichever machine makes it.

maintenance.why: Scale cuts output. Use citric acid and rinse well. It also restores the clean taste of the ice.
It flushes the reservoir. Run it weekly to flush the lines. Skipping it lets film build on the lines.
Standing water grows biofilm. Dry the bin and leave the lid open. Wipe the bin before storing it.
Seals can collect residue. Wipe with a soft cloth. A thin film on the seal is the first sign of buildup.

faq.q: Is nugget ice better than bullet ice?
faq.a: It is softer and chewable. Bullet ice is harder and melts slower. It is the same ice, called by different names. Taste and texture are the real deciding factors. Bullet suits slower sipping and nugget suits chewing.
Louder than bullet makers because of the auger. The crunch of ice dropping in the bin is as noticeable as the hum. Place it where background noise covers the hum.
It stops when full. Disconnect it if you leave for a long trip. It idles with a full bin and restarts when you remove ice.
In hard-water areas, yes. A cheap filter pitcher is the easy fix. Scale on the cylinder is the common reason output drops.
Plan for the footprint plus several inches of clearance. Several inches on each side keeps the compressor cool. A full footprint plus clearance is easy to underestimate.
Between 5 and 10 minutes. Later cycles repeat on a similar clock. Later cycles repeat on a similar clock.
